body:
I discovered the issue. In the angular.json build section I have:
            "assets": [
              "src/favicon.ico",
 
The static folder gets created when I initially start build-storybook. It creates a folder named favicon.ico to include this asset. Then later when build-story writes it's content to the static folder it fails when it tries to copy the Storybook favicon.ico. That results in the error.
 
IMO, this is a bug and should cause a failure.
@dickerstu so what would the desired behavior be exactly?

@dickerstu Does the path you omitted happen to have a `)` character anywhere in it?

I created a new project in my junk `tmp` folder, to tryout a PR, and got an error on saying that the `C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\@storybook\core-server\dist\cjs\public\favicon.ico` file didn't exist. At the time I just ignored it, because I was just in a throw away project and not really testing `build-storybook` anyway. This issue made me go back and take a look at the error I got.

If you don't think the following is related to this issue then can you provide some more information, such as maybe your OS, full path to project, and maybe a repro.

Using Angular `10.2.4` and `12.2.0` and various Storybook versions from `6.3.12` to `6.4.0-rc.5`, I got the following error. It is about a `favicon.ico`, but the error isn't the same, so I don't know if it is a coincidence that both errors deal with a `favicon.ico` or if they are related.
```sh
info => Cleaning outputDir: C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\storybook-static
ERR! NestedError: Cannot copy `C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\@storybook\core-server\dist\cjs\public\favicon.ico`: the file doesn't exist
ERR!     at C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\cpy\index.js:96:10
ERR!     at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
ERR!     at async buildStaticStandalone (C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\@storybook\core-server\dist\cjs\build-static.js:94:3)
ERR!     at async Object.buildStatic (C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\@storybook\core-server\dist\cjs\build-static.js:195:5)
ERR!  NestedError: Cannot copy `C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\@storybook\core-server\dist\cjs\public\favicon.ico`: the file doesn't exist
ERR!     at C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\cpy\index.js:96:10
ERR!     at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
ERR!     at async Object.buildStatic (C:\Users\Mark\dev_home\tmp\New folder (12)\New folder (6)\example-current\node_modules\@storybook\core-server\dist\cjs\build-static.js:195:5) {
ERR!   nested: undefined,
ERR!   name: 'CpyError'
ERR! }
npm ERR! code ELIFECYCLE
npm ERR! errno 1
npm ERR! example-current@0.0.0 build-storybook: `npm run docs:json && build-storybook`
npm ERR! Exit status 1
```

I think I narrowed my problem down to `cpy` not recognizing files if there is a `)` anywhere in the source path. The following stackblitz shows my current progress tracking down the problem. Tomorrow I may dig deeper and see if the problem is with `cpy` or one of it's dependencies.
https://stackblitz.com/edit/node-raizyx?file=package.json

@Marklb The path didn't have a ) in the source path. But I do agree that the problem is with cpy https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/652739548ddb76fd8aab795ea8b52116c78d8630/lib/core-server/src/build-static.ts#L59

@shilman The favicon.ico file is a non-essential file. If Storybook's favicon.ico file required by Storybook for the static build, then I would expect 1) Storybook to overwrite any file or folder named the same and put a warning in the log or 2) ignore and continue. Since this issue isn't breaking the build to run storybook then it shouldn't break the static build.

@dickerstu Do you have a repo that reproduces the problem that you can share? In my projects, there is no problem with the static build, other than my different previously commented problem, and I also still have "src/favicon.ico" in my assets.
@Marklb Sorry, this is my company's app so I won't be able to share it. When you start the build do you not see it immediately being copied into storybook-static?

@dickerstu Yes, the Storybook `favicon.ico` gets copied to the folder and it gets replaced by the one defined in my `angular.json` "assets" when it's done building.

> It creates a folder named favicon.ico to include this asset. 

I just noticed that you said it creates a folder named "favicon.ico". Do you mean that it creates the "favicon.ico" file in the created "storybook-static" folder?

> Then later when build-story writes it's content to the static folder it fails when it tries to copy the Storybook favicon.ico. That results in the error.

Are you sure it fails when copying the Storybook "favicon.ico" or your Angular app's "favicon.ico"?

Are you passing any arguments to "build-storybook"?

Do you have a custom webpack config or customize in the config with `webpackFinal` in `.storybook/main.(js|ts)`?

Do you use Nx or just Angular's cli?

Can you provide the OS and maybe if you have anything open at the time of building that may have any interaction with that folder? This may not matter, but on Windows if I have a project open in VSCode when a script tries to delete a file then I sometimes get an error that the file can't be deleted. Your error is different, but just trying to narrow it down in some way, until the problem can be reproduced.

If fails when copying the Storybook "favicon.ico". 
The build actually created a folder named favicon.ico and placed a copy of the Angular asset favicon.ico within it.
I am not passing any arguments.
No changes to the webpack.config.
I am using Angular's CI.
This is running on Ubuntu-20-04.

@dickerstu I assumed the "src/favicon.ico" in your "assets" was a file, like it is by default in a newly generated Angular CLI project, but is it a folder in your project? When I replaced "src/favicon.ico" file with a folder then I got your error, because Angular ran into a conflict trying to overwrite Storybook's "favicon.ico" file with the "favicon.ico" folder defined in the `angular.json` "assets".

If this is your problem, then I guess this is potentially a Storybook bug, not an Angular bug. I am not sure how best to solve that. I am not sure what the correct solution would be. Normally I assume "favicon.ico" should be a file in the root, but it doesn't have to be, so maybe Storybook should account for that. Someone more familiar with the build process may can answer better, but I am not sure if there is currently a framework independent way to add the favicon after the framework build finishes and write it to an alternate location/name or if that is even a good idea.
